summary: 52-year-old man with confirmed acute cholecystitis on ultrasound; no WBC or CRP on file.

inputs.hpi: Two days of constant right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal with nausea. Known gallstones.

exam.abdomen: Tender right upper quadrant, Murphy's sign positive.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Thick-walled gallbladder (5 mm) with gallstones and pericholecystic fluid. CBD 5 mm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute calculous cholecystitis — early laparoscopic cholecystectomy planned.

top.note: TG18 needs the WBC (and CRP) to diagnose and grade; the value is not in the record, so it is listed rather than pre-filled.

mustExclude.note: The ultrasound report is on file.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Systemic signs (fever, raised CRP, raised WBC) and imaging; Grade II: WBC > 18,000/mm³
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

rationale: Owner's example: cholecystitis without a WBC — the TG18 input first.

authoring.author: Claude (whats-missing)
authoring.notes: What's missing strip vignette. Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy).
